title: PRTremote: Extract PRT Cookies Remotely with InteractiveToken Scheduled Tasks
summary: An InteractiveToken scheduled task and BrowserCore.exe are enough to pull a live PRT cookie off a remote host over SMB.
excerpt: Primary Refresh Tokens are the backbone of Entra ID Single Sign-On (SSO), with each one belonging to a single Windows logon session. Extracting one has traditionally meant getting code running inside that session: process injection or token theft, both heavily signatured, and both requiring malicious code to execute on the endpoint.

title: klist.exe Revisited: Internals and Further Use Cases

summary: A follow-up on klist.exe: extracting non-zeroed TGT session keys without SeTcbPrivilege, abusing WinRM for in-memory remote dumping, and examining behavior under Credential Guard.

title: Abusing klist.exe for Kerberos Post-Exploitation
summary: Running as SYSTEM, the klist.exe that ships with Windows will dump every logged-on user's TGT. I convert them to ccache and build a TGT harvester out of scheduled tasks.

title: Password Spraying ManageEngine and Other RSA-protected Logins
summary: A ManageEngine login on a recent pentest RSA-encrypted every password. Pulling the public key out of the page's JavaScript made it sprayable again.

title: Extending Wazuh with Sysmon and LDAP
summary: Domain controllers don't log LDAP queries by default. I turned that on, wrote Wazuh rules for suspicious queries alongside Sysmon, and caught my own BloodHound run.

title: Bookmarklets as XSS Attack Vectors
